summary: Kimmo Koskenniemi (born 1945) works in computational linguistics. He studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu and the University of Helsinki (MSc 1964–1967), where he later served as Professor of Computer Linguistics (~1989–2012) and BAULT research community director (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Fudan University (MPhil 2005–2008) and the University of Leipzig under Eli Franco (PhD 2009–2018), and held research posts at Leipzig, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and CUHK.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD from the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva (1931–2021) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at the University of London (~1959–1962) and served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (~1969–1995).

Kirby Flower Smith (1862–1918) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Bloomfield, Gildersleeve, and Warren. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and directed the ASCSA Rome.
Kirill Solonin (born 1969) is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He has held professorships at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) and Renmin University of China (~2013).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli (1848–1908) was an Indology scholar who completed his studies at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kishor Chaudhari works in Indology and religious studies. He earned a master's in English from Kavayitri Bahinabai Chaudhari North Maharashtra University in 2013 and became an Assistant Professor at Government Science College, Chhota Udepur in 2018.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under traditional and academic teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, Narmada Tarkatirtha, Panchanana Sastri, Gopinath Bhattacharya, Narayana Chandra Gosvami Nyāyācārya, and Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, and held a post at Calcutta University.

Kitaro Nishida (1870–1945) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz and earned a doctorate from Kyoto University, where he served as Professor of Philosophy from 1910 to 1928.

Kiyoaki Okuda (born 1938) is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973) and served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1993) and director of Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato (1907–1956) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a BA at Otani University (1927–1931) under Enga Teramoto, and later held posts at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).

Kiyoshi Miki (1897–1945) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920) and later held academic posts at Otani University (~1924–1927) and Ryukoku University.

Kiyoshi Okano (born 1956) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University, including assistant professor (attested 2002) and professor of Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He held positions at Rissho University (attested 1990, 2001) and at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 2001).

Kiyoshi Yabuuchi (1906–2000) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and later held academic posts at Kyoto University (~1935–1969) and Ryukoku University (~1969–1979).

Kiyotaka Kimura (born 1940) studied Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo, Shitennoji University, and ICPBS, and was President of Tsurumi Women's University (~2003–2011).

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu (born 1955) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1980–1989) and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1986–1989), later serving as associate professor at Hokkaido University (~1993–2005) and professor at Tohoku University (~2005–2020).

Kiyozo Kazama (born 1928) is a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He taught at Nagoya, Tokyo (~1969–1989), and Hosei (~1989–1999) universities.
